summary: The article provides a generally reliable overview of SGB 2018-19 Series III redemption, but some tax implications have changed recently, making certain claims outdated.

claims.claim: The Sovereign Gold Bond (SGB) 2018-19 Series III has completed its eight-year tenure and is being redeemed today, November 13, 2026.
claims.note: The SGB 2018-19 Series III was issued on November 13, 2018, and has an 8-year tenure, making November 13, 2026, its maturity date.

claims.claim: The SGB 2018-19 Series III was issued in November 2018 at an issue price of ₹3,183 per gram.
claims.note: The issue price for SGB 2018-19 Series III was ₹3,183 per gram, with a ₹50 discount for online applications, making it ₹3,133 per gram for digital payments.

claims.claim: The redemption price for SGBs is determined by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) based on the average closing price of 999 purity gold over the last three business days.
claims.note: The RBI calculates the redemption price based on the simple average of the closing price of 999 purity gold, published by the India Bullion and Jewellers Association (IBJA) Ltd., for the last three business days preceding the redemption date.

claims.claim: For individual investors, the capital gains arising from the redemption of SGBs after the full eight-year maturity period are completely exempt from income tax.
claims.note: Capital gains on SGBs redeemed at maturity (after 8 years) are exempt from tax for individual investors.

claims.claim: If an investor opts for early redemption after the fifth year but before maturity, the capital gains are still considered long-term. In this case, the gains are taxable at 20% after indexation benefits.
claims.note: As per Budget 2026 (effective April 1, 2026), capital gains from premature redemption (after 5 years) are now taxable at a flat 12.5% without indexation benefits for original subscribers. For those who bought from the secondary market, even holding till maturity does not provide tax exemption anymore.

claims.claim: If SGBs are sold on a stock exchange before the eight-year maturity: If sold within three years of purchase, any gains are considered Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG) and are taxed at the investor's applicable income tax slab rate. If sold after three years but before eight years, any gains are considered Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) and are taxed at 20% with indexation benefits.
claims.note: For SGBs sold on a stock exchange, if held for less than 12 months, gains are STCG and taxed at the slab rate. If held for more than 12 months, gains are LTCG and taxed at 12.5% without indexation benefits (effective from April 1, 2026). The 3-year holding period for LTCG and 20% tax with indexation is generally for unlisted securities or certain other assets, not listed SGBs.

claims.claim: The interest income earned on SGBs, which is paid semi-annually, is taxable. This interest is added to the investor's total income and taxed at their applicable income tax slab rate. However, no Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) is applicable on the interest paid on SGBs.
claims.note: Interest from SGBs is taxable at the investor's slab rate and is added to their 'Income from Other Sources'. There is no TDS on SGB interest.

article_title: SGB 2018-19 Series III Redemption: Understanding Your Gold Bond Returns
